/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 10 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2862 (8)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4457 (-2)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2075 (38)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1806 (-4)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1031 (6)
CAPESIZE
Despite a relatively healthy level of operator demand and a couple of tenders circulating, the market finished marginally softer overall, with the BCI 182 5TC slipping just $19 to settle at $40,420. The C5 index eased by $0.210 to $13.590, while C3 also edged lower, losing $0.232 to close at $36.286. In the Pacific, sentiment was slightly softer, with just one miner active in the market. Early indications saw an operator bidding around $13.75, against offers generally in the low $14s. However, the sole miner initially tested the market with a lower bid of $13.00, waiting for offers to soften. As the day progressed, offers gradually moved down to $14.00 and below, with a couple of fixtures eventually reported at $13.50 and $13.60, marginally below yesterday's $13.80 levels. Activity from South Brazil and West Africa to China was slower to develop, with limited activity. C3 bids were generally heard around the low-to-mid $35s, although offers remained predominantly in the mid-$36s. The North Atlantic provided a more positive counterbalance, with sentiment remaining bullish following four fresh Trans-atlantic cargoes. Better bids were being discussed, helping the C8 index climb by around $1,500 to $45,469. Overall, the market was little changed on the day, with a marginal correction in the Pacific and South Atlantic offset by continued strength in the North Atlantic.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic maintained its positive momentum today, with further improvements in the North Atlantic continuing to underpin the wider market. Brokers reported a healthy volume of trans-Atlantic enquiry, particularly from NC South America and the US Gulf, with prompt requirements continuing to command a premium from Owners. Market sources suggested that immediate requirements were facing a tightening supply of workable tonnage, while Charterers with greater flexibility on dates appeared less inclined to chase the market higher. Fronthaul activity remained comparatively limited, with rates showing little meaningful movement despite owners maintaining firm expectations. Market sources described EC South America as continuing to benefit from a relatively tight early December tonnage count, although the availability of ships towards the end of November could limit further gains. Meanwhile, the Pacific remained largely unchanged, with limited fresh activity and a cautious approach from market participants keeping rates broadly stable. Australian mineral enquiry provided some interest, while North Pacific activity offered little fresh direction. The Star Emerald (82,063 2019) open Longkou 12 November was said to have been placed on subjects, while the Shen Hua 803 (75,403 2013) Zhangzhou 17 November was also reported on subjects to Starry Bulk for a minimum 90 to maximum 120 days at $17,500. Overall, the Atlantic remained the driving force behind today’s gains, with the P5TC advancing $342 to close at $18,672.
SUPRAMAX
More of a mixed bag today, North America continues strengthening with more November enquiry emerging, with Charterers having to pay up to tempt Owners into transatlantic trades. The South Atlantic appears to have turned the corner now with rates bottoming out amid a better balance between supply/demand, which is also evident on the larger Panamax stems too. The Continent and Mediterranean are also said to remain tight for tonnage, so in general the Atlantic looks better now, and a Supramax was said to have fixed via the Continent to West Africa in the low $20,000’s, but there were no further details available. In comparison Asia seems to softening in lacklustre trading, despite some strong backhauls being reported today, sources said these were concluded last week. The Medi Balto (63,500 2026) Nantong 9-13 November fixed a trip via Gulf of Aden/Suez to the Black Sea with steels at $35,000 with ITG and the Great Progress (63,377 2015) Dalian 7-10 November also fixed steels (2 x 25mts) and deck cargo via Gulf of Aden/Suez to the Mediterranean at $31,200 with Arm Shipping. The Clover (61,377 2013) CJK 14-15 November was apparently on subjects with Amarante for a trip via NoPac to Bangladesh at $22,000 and another Ultramax was said to subjects via North China to the Caribbean including deck/hatch cargo at $23,000, however no further details came to light. The IVS Trader (63,619 2024) in Singapore fixed a trip to West coast India at $24,000 option East coast India at $23,000, possibly with Fortune Bulk, and the Jia De Chang He (56,532 2011) East coast India fixed a trip China with iron ore at around $9,000, but the Charterers remained private. The 11TC average was down just $45 today, to finish at $22,828.
HANDYSIZE
Another quiet day was reported across both basins, with little fresh information emerging. The BHSI rose by 6 points to 1,031, while the 7TC average increased by $105 to settle at $18,560. In the Continent and Mediterranean, trading remained subdued, with largely unchanged fundamentals offering no clear catalyst for movement. Meanwhile, the US Gulf maintained its momentum, with rates discussed well above last-done levels and prompt Owners showing firmer resistance. The UBC Halifax (38,090 2013) open Venezuela was recently reported fixed by Pangaea for a trip with delivery Puerto Nuevo and redelivery South Brazil carrying coal at just under $15,000, although further details were not disclosed. The South Atlantic appeared broadly balanced, with most participants maintaining a positional stance and little movement in rates. Asia also saw a quiet but broadly balanced session, with rates holding steady for the time being.

Iron Ore Commentary
Trading activity picked up considerably in iron ore today, with total IODEX volume reaching 2.063mt, compared with 579.5kt in yesterday's session. Prices softened over the course of the day, with December trading as high as $93.00 before later clearing at $92.30.

Interest in quarterly spreads remained firm, with Q227/Q427 trading 40ktm at $0.40. Late-evening liquidity also emerged in Nov26/Dec26, with 250kt trading at an average of $0.25, alongside 25ktm of Q127/Q227 trading at $0.30.
